title: Foundation 4: define evidence categories, trust models, and exact claims
description:
Define evidence categories across source fidelity, discovery, adjudication support,
deterministic capability, and state integrity, and state exactly what each proves and
does not prove. Different responsibilities may legitimately use different trust models.
Internal discovery telemetry may use producer-owned observations as primitives under
an explicit internal trust model; source-fidelity and capability/state claims may
require stronger independent evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every evidence category names its claim, trust boundary, owner, and explicit non-claims.
- Presence, ownership, candidacy, schema validity, or code-symbol existence cannot substitute for semantic implementation or runtime execution.
- Diagnostic telemetry, source proof, capability execution evidence, finding evidence, and state evidence are not forced into one proof standard.
- Positive absence is permitted only for an explicitly bounded property/population whose denominator makes absence provable.
- Unresolvable/unrecognized input cannot become satisfied through an empty result.
notes:
ADR-0020 authority reconciliation applied 2026-09-10 by eshyra-o9bd.19.6.5.
The operative title/description/acceptance criteria supersede contradictory
pre-ADR global-closure language in older notes. Historical notes remain evidence,
not current authority.
